title: Extractable admin workflows as lightweight services
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Our current runbooks are long-form documents and ad-hoc scripts; on-call and support engineers repeatedly re-run multi-step procedures with slight variations, causing inconsistencies and noisy telemetry. Goal: Convert a set of high-frequency runbook procedures into extractable, versioned, lightweight services ("adminlets") that can be invoked from the Console, CLI, and automation pipelines. Each adminlet should be idempotent, permission-gated, support dry-run and explain modes, and emit structured telemetry and audit events. Deliverable: A small runtime library + service mesh of adminlets, migration guide for existing runbooks, and a Console integration to invoke and review results.
acceptance_criteria: Three canonical runbooks (user-access-reset, allocation-warmup, kv-cache-sweep) implemented as extractable adminlets with documented inputs and outputs
- dry-run mode that returns a deterministic plan without mutating state
- RBAC check hooks connected to our org permissions
- structured audit events compatible with existing audit log schema
CI and e2e tests that simulate oncall flows and validate telemetry and revert behavior
Migration doc and a Console MVP to discover, run, and view adminlet runs within 2 clicks
steps: Design API surface for adminlets (inputs, outputs, failures, retries) - owner: Liam
Prototype local adminlet runner library (Python + Go bindings) and small shim to run inside private deployment - owner: Sienna
Implement 3 pilot adminlets referenced in AC - owners: team leads
Instrument audit + telemetry hooks and add schema to telemetry registry
Build Console action card to list adminlets and launch runs with parameter UI
Create migration runner that can transform selected runbook steps into adminlet invocations
Security review and threat model for adminlet execution surface
Rollout plan with feature flag, canary users, and fallback to original runbook text
